To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a list, based on a combination of experimental and predicted data, of privileged chemical substructure scaffolds and substructures that are often observed within inhibitors targeting protein-protein interactions and that are devoid of any toxicophore and pan-assay interference alerts.
we identified a list of scaffolds and substructures that are privileged to modulate protein-proteins interactions.
we have identified a set of privileged chemical moieties, scaffolds, and substructures that can be used by medicinal chemists to design and synthesize initial quality chemical probes for PPI targets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of privileged chemical substructure that are most often present in PPI inhibitors.
the identification of privileged scaffolds and chemical substructures that have been found in the literature to be active on protein-protein interactions.
the identification of chemical substructures that have been observed to be most often found within PPI inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chemical space of PPI inhibitors is not as limited as previously believed and that a wide range of chemical scaffolds can be used to modulate PPI targets.

the privileged substructures identified in this analysis are not only present within the most active iPPI compounds but are also present within the iPPI compounds that have the most diverse chemical structures.

the privileged substructures identified in this analysis are the ones most often found in inhibitors of protein-protein interactions and that they can be used as starting points to design chemical probes on these challenging targets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the privileged scaffolds identified in this study can be used for the design and synthesis of initial quality iPPI compounds.
the use of molecular frameworks is an efficient way to identify privileged substructures in PPI inhibitors.

privileged substructures to modulate PPIs can be defined as chemical substructures that can be found in the majority of compounds that are able to bind to PPIs and are not known to be toxicophores or pan-assay interference compounds (PAINS).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemical space of iPPI compounds can be substantially expanded by using privileged substructures as chemical scaffolds and chemical functionalization.
privileged chemical substructures can be used to modulate protein-proteins interactions.
privileged substructures are a valuable source of chemical diversity that can be exploited to design chemical probes targeting PPIs.
